artboards.title: A block is what you place

annotations.text: THE CURRENT READING. An archetype owns a vocabulary of slots. The floor archetype's slots are the sixteen corner masks; the wall's are named parts including its seams; the ramp's are parts at a root-2 aspect. There is no universal tag.
OPEN, and the same question twice: does a pairing in a non-floor archetype get a whole block or a single piece? Two wall materials meeting along a run, and a floor meeting the wall beneath it.

Shapes and Seams were drawn while the corner set was still taken as universal. Shapes is right about the fifteen masks and about 16 beating 47; Seams is right that a seam cannot be a corner tag. Both are superseded on whose vocabulary owns what.

Material's art page predates the correction too: it shows a corner block plus named slots for every archetype. Under the current reading a wall material would show only its seven named slots and no corner block at all.
Authoring and Format are the first sketches, kept for the GID scheme and the block geometry. To be redrawn once the model settles.
